configuration.stream_order: phases I->II->III; within a phase ordered by (capture timestamp, camera id, path)
labels_allowed_for: offline metadata diagnostics and query-composition reporting

physical_object_rule.physical_object: Real-IAD sample directory S#### beneath the class root; all camera views and all OK/NG capture sessions of one sample share the identity
physical_object_rule.camera_observation: one original image; (sample, capture session, camera id, timestamp)
physical_object_rule.capture_session: OK or NG_<DEFECT>; multiple sessions per sample are different photographing rounds of the same product
physical_object_rule.legacy_v02_group: the historical token <class>_<NNNN>_<STATE>[_<DEFECT>] = sample + session, therefore NOT a physical object
physical_object_rule.image_label: anomaly_class == OK for that single image; never propagated to sibling views
physical_object_rule.query_unit: one image-level label per physical object per stream
validated_by: sample directory S#### must agree with the numeric file token
directory layout must agree with the encoded OK/NG session
capture timestamp must be a valid YYYYMMDDHHMMSS
no duplicate image path or file name within a class

known_dataset_findings.finding: Real-IAD's released train/test JSONs share physical sample ids; the same product can appear as a train (OK) photo and as a test (NG) photo
known_dataset_findings.consequence: train-derived support/history samples must be reserved out of the test pool, which D1-A does

known_dataset_findings.finding: the historical V0.2 unit was sample + capture session, so the 525 'objects' represent far fewer products
known_dataset_findings.consequence: the historical unique-object audit fraction of 15.05% overstates true object coverage

known_dataset_findings.finding: under true physical identity the historical V0.2 split places the same sample in a train-derived partition and in a test partition
known_dataset_findings.consequence: V0.2 numbers are retained as history and are not reinterpreted; D1-A builds a disjoint partition

known_dataset_findings.finding: the historical one-label-per-group rule could charge two labels to two sessions of one physical sample
known_dataset_findings.consequence: Q-A charges at most one label per physical object

known_dataset_findings.finding: images from defective capture sessions are individually labelled OK when that camera view shows no defect
known_dataset_findings.consequence: image-level labels are never propagated across views; probes keep image-level truth

claim_boundaries: D1-A reports metadata feasibility only; no anomaly-detection metric and no admission result is computed
the official Real-IAD split is not physical-object disjoint, so this partition reserves every support/history sample explicitly
one image-level label is charged per physical object per stream
